root_cause: (1) e2e identities are salted per spec FILE only, so every test of dm-pairing-pending-confirmation, every --repeat-each repeat/retry and every run on a non-wiped relay shared one USER_A/USER_B pair; on confirm the app correctly reveals ALL held DMs from B on the relay, including earlier runs' (count 5/7/11 instead of 2). Test-isolation defect, not a product defect. (2) dm-historical-recovery hand-signed back-dated gift wraps in the test process and wrote them to strfry over raw WebSocket. (3) The dev-only __fewPublishDm bridge lived in unreadStore.ts.
fix: auth-helpers.ts: computeTestKeypairs({ perTest: true }) additionally salts with testId + repeatEachIndex + retry + randomUUID (opt-in; refused for UNSALTED_SPEC_FILES; default unchanged). All 8 dm-pairing-* specs switched beforeAll(computeTestKeypairs()) -> beforeEach(computeTestKeypairs({ perTest: true })); exact count assertions kept. dm-historical-recovery: Alice's page is closed, Bob sends 5 DMs through his own app page via __fewPublishDm (>1 s apart for distinct rumor seconds), Alice reopens and must render exactly 5 in order [0..4] (was >=5 / non-strict), dedup on reopen unchanged; no test-process publish, nostr-tools/nip59 and raw WS removed. Bridge moved verbatim to app/src/lib/dmPublishTestBridge.ts (same name, same guards), side-effect-imported from pages/_app.tsx.
deviations_from_design: dm-giftwrap-bell already used the bridge and dm-third-party-inbound no longer exists; only dm-historical-recovery needed rewriting, and it needed no narrow exception (no fixture loader created).
Per-test identities applied to all dm-pairing-* specs (not just pending-confirmation) for uniform history independence; single-test specs were not observed polluted in the gate.

The pending-confirmation spec comment (step 4) says DM content is only persisted once the peer's ContactChat mounts. In dm-historical-recovery, Alice (Bob is a co-member of a group) had 4 of Bob's 5 offline-sent messages stored under few:messages:dm:<bob> right after loading /contacts, before opening the chat. Either some boot-time path persists known-peer DM content or the comment is stale; not investigated further (no assertion depends on it now).

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Two of the three specs named in the publish-via-app finding had already been fixed or deleted, and the finding still referenced the pre-rebrand bridge name (__nostlingPublishDm); verifying against code first saved a pointless rewrite. A spec comment's claim about when DM content gets persisted was not true for a group-member peer, which cost one e2e cycle on a precondition built on it.
